doc: The feed-forward network, built from an explicit JSON spec so the forward pass is arithmetic anyone can check by hand rather than a number to trust. It reads no file, so nothing here can be skipped for want of data. Until the R and Java modules gained NeuralNet.i this could only be tested in two languages.

cases.doc: Two layers with known weights. [1, 2] through a 3x2 relu layer gives [0.5, 1.1, 1.7] -- all positive, so relu is the identity here -- and summing those with a bias of 0.5 gives 3.8. A binding that transposed the weight matrix would get a different, equally plausible number, which is why the weights are asymmetric.
The same network with a negative input. The first layer's outputs go negative and relu floors them at zero, so the answer is the bias alone -- the one case that tells relu apart from the identity.
